observations.seen: The 'Marine Dusk' sky preset is active, but the scene reads as flat, neutral daylight. A warm glow appears only at the far horizon. There is no low, directional golden-hour key light raking across the facades or the road.
The player robotaxi's white body is near-clipped with almost no form shading, so its volume reads as a flat white cutout.

Buildings, the cable car and the player car cast no clear directional shadows. The player car has no visible contact shadow grounding it. The only ground darkening is a faint patch under the parked sedan at left.
The player car's white paint and black rear glass show no environment reflections, specular highlights or fresnel. Building windows are dark flat texture and do not reflect the sky.
Brick-textured mid-rise blocks, sidewalks, overhead wires, cable car tracks and lane markings give a readable San Francisco street. The facades are repeated flat textures with little parallax depth.

Light distance haze softens the end of the street. There is no volumetric light, no sun shafts and no warm fog falloff in the 30–180 m range. The amber pool on the road is the only atmospheric accent.

The player vehicle shows jagged, noisy silhouette edges, which look like alpha or texture-seam artifacts. Its paint has no roughness or clearcoat variation. The asphalt is a uniform dark plane with no wear or wetness.
The tree at right is a primitive green sphere on a thin cylinder, which clashes with the more detailed cable car and buildings. The robotaxi model is blobby, with low-detail rectangular tail lights.
The player car fills roughly 30–35% of the frame, above the 15–25% target. HUD panels and nametags crowd the top-center vanishing point, where the road and horizon glow should lead the eye.
The chase camera is low, centered and close behind the car. The FOV looks near 60 but slightly tight for the subject size.
No visible bloom on the tail lights or headlight pool, no film grain, no vignette and no color grade toward warm asphalt and burnt orange. Tone mapping clips the white car.

The HUD is cohesive and polished: dark translucent panels, a teal and orange accent palette, a circular minimap, a speedometer arc and a fare card. It is heavily cluttered, though. The debug-style fleet, camera and sky selector bars at the bottom and the rival nametags take up a large share of the play view.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
